title: UDLM Bundle
description: A BUNDLE is one activatable unit: activating it turns on (or off) the capabilities, policies, settings, and mechanisms it names, so a deployment gets the posture appropriate to its use and environment. The record is an INERT, reusable definition — 'which bundle this deployment runs' is deployment state, not a field here. A bundle REFERENCES governed artifacts; it never defines them (content lives in its own artifact, named by URF — identifier-scheme §9). Profiles are bundles: `udlm/profile/dev` is a bundle whose contents are the governance artifacts that profile turns on — a profile is not a distinct record kind (filter, never subtype). ADR-015 (settings and configuration bundles) is the deciding record; ADR-007 supplies the floor semantics preserved in `contains[].state`.

uuid.description: RFC 9562 identity — frozen for the bundle's life (ADR-051).

tenant_uuid.description: Owning tenant for an organization-authored bundle; absent for platform/built-in bundles.

composes.description: Other bundles this one contains, by URF reference. Activation is transitive: activating this bundle activates everything the composed bundles turn on. A composing bundle MUST NOT weaken a composed bundle's `required` entry to `advisory` or `off` — refused at validation (the immutable-ceiling discipline; most-restrictive-wins for security-relevant entries).

contains.description: The flat list of what this bundle turns on or off — one entry per governed artifact, any kind (policy, capability, mechanism, layer, vocabulary). The entry's kind is whatever its reference resolves to; the bundle does not classify it. AN UNLISTED ARTIFACT IS AVAILABLE BUT NOT MANDATED — the ADR-007 floor semantic: a floor is a minimum, never a filter, so omission never means disabled. `off` is the explicit, auditable way to disable.

ref.description: URF reference to the governed artifact this entry governs (identifier-scheme §9).

state.description: required — must be present and enforcing (the floor). advisory — enabled, non-blocking (surfaces findings, does not refuse). off — deliberately disabled in this posture; explicit and auditable, distinct from unlisted.

settings.description: Per-entry configuration for the referenced artifact — the values that tune it in this posture (cadence, mode, thresholds). Values only; the artifact owns its schema.

reason.description: Why this disposition in this posture — required for `off` on a security-relevant artifact so a reviewer sees the intent, not just the absence.

settings.description: Bundle-level configuration values that have no artifact to reference. Values only — a setting whose home is an artifact belongs in that entry's `settings`.

activation.description: Properties OF THE DEFINITION — not deployment state. Which bundle a deployment currently runs is recorded by the deployment, never here.

is_builtin.description: Ships with the substrate (as opposed to organization-authored).

default.description: The out-of-box choice when a deployment selects no bundle.

approved.description: Cleared for activation under the governing review process.

examples.name: Homelab
examples.description: Single-operator posture: the smallest required floor, stronger controls available and one toggle away.

contains.reason: no transparency-log operator in a single-operator lab; append-only audit still required
